findings.title: The compressed opening challenge
findings.claim: The opening asks why this audience has not recognized evidence already before it.
findings.mechanism: The interrogative and connective opening meets past-negated seeing and the fact clause that follows; that contact makes the first words a rebuking challenge to missed recognition rather than a neutral question.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader enters an argument already pressing its audience to account for what it has seen.
findings.containment: The challenge introduces the proof without replacing the proposition that the following clause states.

epistemic.reason: The QAC analysis of the opening particles and two candidate supports agree on a linked recognition question.

findings.title: A failure already in view
findings.claim: The past negation presents nonrecognition as a failure that should already have been corrected.
findings.mechanism: Lam governs the jussive seeing verb; its past-negating force meets the opening question and the following stated evidence, turning present challenge into reproach for a prior missed recognition.
findings.reader_payoff: The question presses on an opportunity already supplied by the creation proof.
findings.containment: This temporal pressure qualifies the audience's failure to see; it does not identify every person's motive.

epistemic.reason: QAC supplies the jussive relation and the candidate evidence specifies its retrospective force.

findings.title: Seeing as considered recognition
findings.claim: The plural seeing verb can carry considered judgment because the question places a complete creation claim before its audience.
findings.mechanism: The proposition introduced after the seeing verb names the created heavens and earth and the Creator's capacity; this independent content gives the verb a judgment-bearing contact alongside physical perception.
findings.reader_payoff: The opening can be heard as asking for recognition of an inference, while its ordinary seeing sense remains available.
findings.containment: The judgment reading is qualified by the supplied cognitive range and local proposition; it does not erase sight.

epistemic.reason: The word analysis explicitly preserves physical and cognitive seeing, and the focus proposition supplies the trigger for the latter.
